claim: For the natural action of \(S_4\) permuting the vertices of the tetrahedron \(\Delta^3\), the rational \(S_4\)-module \(H_4(\mathcal M(\Delta^3);\mathbb Q)\) has character values \((99,1,-1,0,-1)\) on the cycle types \((1^4),(2,1^2),(2^2),(3,1),(4)\). Consequently, \[H_4(\mathcal M(\Delta^3);\mathbb Q)\cong 4S^{(4)}\oplus13S^{(3,1)}\oplus8S^{(2,2)}\oplus12S^{(2,1,1)}\oplus4S^{(1,1,1,1)}.\]

correctness.rationale: Exhaustive reconstruction gives the established face vector. A complete acyclic matching on the Morse complex leaves one critical 0-cell, two critical 3-cells, and 101 critical 4-cells; the exact signed Morse boundary has a unit full-rank 2-by-2 minor, so reduced homology is \(\mathbb Z^{99}\) only in degree \(4\). Signed chain traces for representatives of all five \(S_4\) conjugacy classes are then computed directly; equivariant Euler--Poincare gives character \((99,1,-1,0,-1)\), and exact character inner products give multiplicities \((4,13,8,12,4)\).

value.rationale: The tetrahedral Morse complex is a canonical benchmark repeatedly singled out in the literature. Its known rank-99 homology and nonequivariant wedge type leave the natural tetrahedral symmetry completely unresolved. The exact decomposition into all five irreducible \(S_4\)-types is a substantive symmetry refinement with direct relevance to equivariant topology and fixed-point/Lefschetz analyses; it is not a relabeling or arbitrary parameter slice.
